newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: YACHTING-BRITISH UNLIKELY TO RACE FOR AMERICA'S CUP.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-BRITISH UNLIKELY TO RACE FOR AMERICA'S CUP.

text.p: The British beat the big guns of yachting to sail against Team New Zealand for the mini America's Cup but they may not even compete for the real thing in 1999, skipper Chris Law said on Sunday.
"I can't see how all the pieces will fit together," said Law, who sailed for The Royal Dorset Yacht Club in the final of the mini-cup regatta on Auckland's Waitemata Harbour on Sunday.

The British challengers lost to the New Zealand boat Black Magic four races to one but they earned a lot of respect for beating teams from New York, San Francisco and France to take on the America's Cup champions.
In spite of their efforts, Law said it was difficult to persuade British companies to back a challenge for the America's Cup.

"History is a factor," he said. "The America's Cup has a stigma about it in England -- pink gins, double-breasted blazers and (former Prime Minister) Ted Heath. Yet none of the guys on the boat had private education. They're all everyday blokes."
Law, who sailed for Sydney 95 in the 1992 America's Cup, said he was looking at other syndicates for the next regatta although his preference would be to sail for Britain.
